paragraphs.source_en: That day was the Bon Festival, when countless souls were said to return from the spirit world to visit family and friends among the living; yet on that very day, Hidetsugu was bound for the realm of the dead. As for his three young attendants—Yamamoto Tonomo, Yamada Sanjūrō, and Fuwa Bansaku—no matter how Hidetsugu tried to dissuade them, they too resolved to follow him in death, and all three set out upon the road to the underworld before him.

paragraphs.source_en: No sooner had Hidetsugu finished speaking than Yamamoto Tonomo became the first to drive a dagger into his belly. paragraphs.source_en: When Tokugawa Ieyasu once again came to the capital from Edo, it was already the ninth day after Hidetsugu’s suicide: the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month in the fourth year of Bunroku. By then Toyotomi Hideyoshi had already begun putting Hidetsugu’s retainers to death one after another with extraordinary cruelty. Kimura Hitachi-no-suke committed seppuku at Ibaraki; his son Shima-no-suke fled to Kitayama in Kyoto and, upon learning of his father’s death, killed himself at Shōgyōji in Teramachi. Kumagai Daizen committed seppuku at Nison-in in Saga, Shirai Bingo-no-kami died at Daiun-in in Shijō, and Awa Moku-no-kami took his own life in Higashiyama—Hidetsugu’s dream was utterly destroyed.

paragraphs.source_zh: 德川家康再次从江户进京，已是秀次自尽后第九日，文禄四年七月二十四。此时丰臣秀吉已异常残酷地把秀次的家臣一个个处死。木村常陆介在茨木切腹，其子志摩介则逃亡到京城的北山，在得知其父死讯后，到寺町的正行寺自尽。熊谷大膳于嵯峨的二尊院切腹，白井备后守在四条院的大云院死去，阿波木工头则于东山自裁——秀次的梦完全破灭。

paragraphs.source_en: The cruelty with which Hideyoshi handled the affair seemed almost beyond comprehension. Yet Ieyasu and his son had foreseen such an outcome from the very beginning.

units.source_en: The cruelty with which Hideyoshi handled the affair seemed almost beyond comprehension.
units.source_zh: 秀吉如此残酷地处理此事，让人深感不可思议。

units.source_en: Yet Ieyasu and his son had foreseen such an outcome from the very beginning.
units.source_zh: 可一开始，家康父子便已猜测到了这样的结局。

paragraphs.source_zh: 秀吉如此残酷地处理此事，让人深感不可思议。可一开始，家康父子便已猜测到了这样的结局。

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyori was still only a babbling infant held on Hideyoshi’s knee, yet because of him the blood of countless people had already flowed in rivers. Kikutei Harusue, father of Hidetsugu’s concubine Ichinodai, was exiled to Echigo for helping the kanpaku send gold into the imperial palace; and Date Masamune, because he had frequently visited the kanpaku’s residence, likewise came close to the ruin of his entire house.

units.source_en: Hideyori was still only a babbling infant held on Hideyoshi’s knee, yet because of him the blood of countless people had already flowed in rivers.
units.source_zh: 此时秀赖还只是一个被秀吉抱在膝上、咿呀学语的婴孩，可是因为他，无数人的鲜血已经流成了河。

units.source_en: Kikutei Harusue, father of Hidetsugu’s concubine Ichinodai, was exiled to Echigo for helping the kanpaku send gold into the imperial palace;
units.source_zh: 秀次的侧室一御台之父菊亭晴季，由于帮着关白把黄金送到宫里，被流放到越后；

units.source_en: and Date Masamune, because he had frequently visited the kanpaku’s residence, likewise came close to the ruin of his entire house.

ja.t: ぼされるところだった。

units.source_zh: 伊达政宗由于频繁出入关白官邸，也差点家破人亡。

paragraphs.source_zh: 此时秀赖还只是一个被秀吉抱在膝上、咿呀学语的婴孩，可是因为他，无数人的鲜血已经流成了河。秀次的侧室一御台之父菊亭晴季，由于帮着关白把黄金送到宫里，被流放到越后；伊达政宗由于频繁出入关白官邸，也差点家破人亡。

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu went to extraordinary lengths to save Masamune from destruction. He told Hideyoshi that if Masamune were executed now, Ōshū would inevitably be plunged into great turmoil. Negotiations with the Great Ming had yet to produce a result, and such a step, he warned, could only provoke civil war within Japan. At last Hideyoshi accepted Ieyasu’s counsel.

units.source_en: Ieyasu went to extraordinary lengths to save Masamune from destruction.
units.source_zh: 家康为了让政宗免遭灭顶之灾，可谓大费苦心。

units.source_en: He told Hideyoshi that if Masamune were executed now, Ōshū would inevitably be plunged into great turmoil.
units.source_zh: 他告诉秀吉，若现在处决政宗，奥州势将陷入大乱。

units.source_en: Negotiations with the Great Ming had yet to produce a result, and such a step, he warned, could only provoke civil war within Japan.

ja.t: がついておらず、そのような

units.source_zh: 眼下和大明国的谈判还没有结果，一旦如此，恐只会引发日本内乱。

units.source_en: At last Hideyoshi accepted Ieyasu’s counsel.
units.source_zh: 秀吉终于接受了家康的谏言。

paragraphs.source_zh: 家康为了让政宗免遭灭顶之灾，可谓大费苦心。他告诉秀吉，若现在处决政宗，奥州势将陷入大乱。眼下和大明国的谈判还没有结果，一旦如此，恐只会引发日本内乱。秀吉终于接受了家康的谏言。

paragraphs.source_en: “Very well, I shall let you keep your head for now. This is the second time. If there is a third, feel your neck first.” Hideyoshi, never one to guard his tongue, gave Masamune a savage dressing-down; from that moment, Masamune sided with Ieyasu from the bottom of his heart.

units.source_en: “Very well, I shall let you keep your head for now. This is the second time. If there is a third, feel your neck first.”

ja.t: はつないでおいてやる。これで

units.source_zh: “好，我暂且把你的头留着，这可是第二次了，再有第三次，先摸摸你的脑袋吧。”

units.source_en: Hideyoshi, never one to guard his tongue, gave Masamune a savage dressing-down; from that moment, Masamune sided with Ieyasu from the bottom of his heart.
units.source_zh: 秀吉口无遮拦，把政宗斥责了一顿，这让政宗从心底站到了家康一边。

paragraphs.source_zh: “好，我暂且把你的头留着，这可是第二次了，再有第三次，先摸摸你的脑袋吧。”秀吉口无遮拦，把政宗斥责了一顿，这让政宗从心底站到了家康一边。

paragraphs.source_en: The Taikō now devoted himself to spreading terror. He was utterly deaf to the admonitions of the Kita-no-Mandokoro and to the efforts of Ieyasu and Toshiie to stop him. “If this continues, it will surely bring disaster upon Hideyori in years to come.” Even warnings such as this fell on deaf ears.

units.source_en: The Taikō now devoted himself to spreading terror.
units.source_zh: 如今的太阁致力于制造恐怖之气。

units.source_en: He was utterly deaf to the admonitions of the Kita-no-Mandokoro and to the efforts of Ieyasu and Toshiie to stop him.
units.source_zh: 北政所的劝诫、家康和利家的阻止，他根本就听不进去。

units.source_en: “If this continues, it will surely bring disaster upon Hideyori in years to come.”
units.source_zh: “照此下去，日后必会为秀赖带来灾难。”

units.source_en: Even warnings such as this fell on deaf ears.
units.source_zh: 甚至连这样的劝诫，他也充耳不闻。

paragraphs.source_zh: 如今的太阁致力于制造恐怖之气。北政所的劝诫、家康和利家的阻止，他根本就听不进去。“照此下去，日后必会为秀赖带来灾难。”甚至连这样的劝诫，他也充耳不闻。

paragraphs.source_en: Bleak autumn winds swept every street and alley of the capital, and at last, on the second day of the eighth month, Hideyoshi had more than thirty of Hidetsugu’s wives, concubines, and children taken under guard to the riverbank at Sanjō. Had Hidetsugu still been alive, what would he have thought at the sight of his wives and children being marched to the Sanjō riverbank? Surely he would have ground his teeth with hatred and bitterly regretted failing to see the true heart of his own uncle.

units.source_en: Bleak autumn winds swept every street and alley of the capital, and at last, on the second day of the eighth month, Hideyoshi had more than thirty of Hidetsugu’s wives, concubines, and children taken under guard to the riverbank at Sanjō.
units.source_zh: 萧瑟的秋风吹遍京城的大街小巷，秀吉最终还是于八月初二，令人把秀次的妻妾及子女共三十余人押赴三条河滩。

units.source_en: Had Hidetsugu still been alive, what would he have thought at the sight of his wives and children being marched to the Sanjō riverbank?
units.source_zh: 若秀次还活着，看到被押赴三条河的妻儿，不知会作何感想。

units.source_en: Surely he would have ground his teeth with hatred and bitterly regretted failing to see the true heart of his own uncle.
units.source_zh: 他定会恨得咬牙切齿，后悔没看清亲舅父的心肠。

paragraphs.source_zh: 萧瑟的秋风吹遍京城的大街小巷，秀吉最终还是于八月初二，令人把秀次的妻妾及子女共三十余人押赴三条河滩。若秀次还活着，看到被押赴三条河的妻儿，不知会作何感想。他定会恨得咬牙切齿，后悔没看清亲舅父的心肠。

paragraphs.source_en: The Hideyoshi of old had been powerful and decisive. With mighty self-assurance he judged all things, ruled all things, and stood resolute amid the surging waves. But once anxiety closed around him, he exposed his weakness completely.

units.source_en: The Hideyoshi of old had been powerful and decisive.
units.source_zh: 从前的秀吉强大而果断。

units.source_en: With mighty self-assurance he judged all things, ruled all things, and stood resolute amid the surging waves.
units.source_zh: 他有强大的自信裁决一切，支配一切，毅然挺立于波涛之中。

units.source_en: But once anxiety closed around him, he exposed his weakness completely.

ja.t: りつかれてからというもの、その

units.source_zh: 然而，他自从被不安笼罩，就完全暴露出了弱点。

paragraphs.source_zh: 从前的秀吉强大而果断。他有强大的自信裁决一切，支配一切，毅然挺立于波涛之中。然而，他自从被不安笼罩，就完全暴露出了弱点。

paragraphs.source_en: “Alas. Can the Taikō truly mean to kill even those little children who understand nothing?”

Can the Taikō truly mean to kill even those little children who understand nothing?”

paragraphs.source_zh: “唉。太阁竟连那些不懂事的孩子都要杀掉？”

paragraphs.source_en: “Surely not. How could anyone kill such innocent children? They must be taken somewhere and placed under guard.”

units.source_en: “Surely not. How could anyone kill such innocent children? They must be taken somewhere and placed under guard.”

ja.t: せるものか。きっとどこかへ

units.source_zh: “不会吧，那些天真的孩子怎能杀呢，他们一定会被转移到某处看管起来。”

paragraphs.source_zh: “不会吧，那些天真的孩子怎能杀呢，他们一定会被转移到某处看管起来。”

paragraphs.source_en: “Yes—just look how innocent they are…”

units.source_en: “Yes—just look how innocent they are…”

paragraphs.source_zh: “是啊，你看，孩子们多天真……”

paragraphs.source_en: Spectators thronged the riverbank like clouds, all silent as they watched the innocent people before them. Because only women and children were to be executed, the guards were not especially strict. Yet before them hung, unmistakably, a head already beginning to rot: Hidetsugu’s head.

units.source_en: Spectators thronged the riverbank like clouds, all silent as they watched the innocent people before them.
units.source_zh: 观者如云，挤满了河滩，人们都默不作声，静静看着这些无辜的人。

units.source_en: Because only women and children were to be executed, the guards were not especially strict.
units.source_zh: 由于是处死妇孺，防守并不严格。

units.source_en: Yet before them hung, unmistakably, a head already beginning to rot: Hidetsugu’s head.
units.source_zh: 可是，他们面前，分明挂着一个已开始腐烂的头颅，那是秀次的头。

paragraphs.source_zh: 观者如云，挤满了河滩，人们都默不作声，静静看着这些无辜的人。由于是处死妇孺，防守并不严格。可是，他们面前，分明挂着一个已开始腐烂的头颅，那是秀次的头。

paragraphs.source_en: Many different explanations were offered for this execution. Some said Hideyoshi wanted the ruffians and outlaws of Kyoto to remember this bloody slaughter, so that no one in the world would ever again dare entertain thoughts of rebellion. Before Hidetsugu’s head, more than ten executioners stood in a line, pouring water over their naked blades. They began calling the prisoners’ names, starting with the children and making each one sit on the ground in turn.

paragraphs.source_en: As they were seated in a row, the young children’s faces lost all color. Even a beast instinctively feels terror when dragged into a slaughterhouse—how much more must a human being feel? Their wails rang out without end, too dreadful to hear.

paragraphs.source_en: Then a great chorus of Buddhist invocations rose over the riverbank. Not only the children’s mothers but all the women awaiting execution raised their voices; it was the last resistance they could offer. The assembled spectators also cried out as one. Naturally, the people’s hatred turned upon the officials who had come to oversee the executions—Ishida Jibu-shōyū and Mashita Uemon-no-jō, seated side by side beneath a pavilion erected on the western bank.
